newsitem.title: UK: London gold tumbles to 3-year lows, seen lower.
newsitem.headline: London gold tumbles to 3-year lows, seen lower.

text.p: Gold was fixed at its lowest in more than three years on Tuesday morning, continuing its sharp decline in prices after taking another beating overnight.
Bullion was set at $369.00 an ounce, the lowest since November 3, 1993 and below the psychological $370 an ounce level. It had fixed at $370.75 on Monday afternoon.
Analysts forecast further weakness for gold as a strong dollar against the mark discouraged buyers, and selling by gold mining houses cast a bearish pall over the market.
"If the dollar keeps going strong we'll have another push to the downside," a dealer said.
Prices sank to a low of around $367.50 an ounce in active Asian trading overnight, after sinking below the $370 an ounce level in New York trading.
A light bounce from those lows was expected to be stalled at around $370 an ounce and smartly turned back to the downside.
"If we breach $367.50, you can name your next number on the downside. The $362-$363 area should provide some support, but that depends on how big and who the seller is," a dealer said.
Physical gold demand, usually at a seasonal peak at this time of year, was virtually absent from the market despite the lower prices, dealers said.
"A lot of people have done their business early and in big numbers, so there's nothing there right now," a dealer said.
Persistant market talk of a central bank selling some of its gold reserves further pressed down on gold, and left professionals in the market struggling to plot gold's next move.
Silver, although inching lower with gold, has nevertheless found support around $4.70 an ounce.
But it too looked destined to further losses down to $4.50-$4.60 if gold's downtrend continued, analysts said.
Platinum followed gold lower and was indicated down $1.25 at $372.00/$373.00.
Ample inventories and selling by investment funds had bloated supply, analysts said, leaving the way open to further losses down to $363 an ounce.
Palladium, however, bucked the trend and rose $0.25 from Monday's finish to $115.00/$116.00.
